answer: Copying the same citations across 123 aliases thus pays the authoring cost 123 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the wharf index resolves every citation against the shale checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the horizon audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 29 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
